faqs.question: Is it too late to start a tutor in Grade 12?
faqs.answer: No, and a grade 12 IB DP home tutoring in Mumbai arrangement started late can still help, but what it can achieve narrows as the year goes on and the plan has to narrow with it. Starting in the autumn leaves room to work on content, technique and the internal work still open. Starting after the mocks means choosing one subject and one weakness and accepting that the others stay where they are. Starting in the final weeks is worth it only for exam technique and for keeping a student working to deadlines. Be suspicious of anyone who tells you that a late start makes no difference, and equally suspicious of anyone who says it is pointless.

faqs.question: Can a tutor change my son's predicted grade?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who suggests otherwise should be removed from your shortlist. The predicted grade is the school's professional judgement, based on internal assessments, mocks and class work. A tutor cannot issue it, revise it or lobby for it. What a tutor can do is change the evidence the school is looking at, by helping the student produce better work that the subject teacher actually sees over several weeks. That is slower and less satisfying than a shortcut, and it is the only legitimate route. If you want the prediction reviewed, that conversation belongs with the subject teacher and the DP coordinator.

faqs.question: Our daughter has a conditional offer that names a specific Higher Level grade. How should we brief the tutor?
faqs.answer: Give the tutor the offer conditions as written, not a summary. Name the subject and the grade required, say what the last school assessment put her on, and state the examination session. Then ask the tutor to tell you whether the gap looks like content or technique, and what the first month would contain. A brief that says improve her Physics produces even, unfocused hours. A brief that says the offer requires a specific Higher Level Physics grade and she is short on Paper technique produces a plan. Keep the admissions side with your college counsellor rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Lower Parel on a Sunday morning?
faqs.answer: Sunday mornings are the easiest slot in the city to fill, so usually yes. Lower Parel and Prabhadevi sit between the Western Line and the Eastern Freeway approaches, and weekend traffic on the Coastal Road and Senapati Bapat Marg bears no resemblance to a weekday evening, which widens the pool considerably. Tell us your tower and the visitor process at your gate when you enquire, since a Sunday pass sometimes needs arranging in advance. For final-year families, a long weekend morning session usually achieves more than two rushed weekday evening ones.

faqs.question: What happens to home tuition during study leave and the examination weeks?
faqs.answer: The pattern should change, and you should agree how before study leave starts. Once the student is at home all day, morning sessions beat evening ones, sessions get shorter and more frequent, and much of the work becomes sitting a timed paper then going through it. Many families move most sessions online at this point so that no time is lost to travel. Ask the tutor in advance whether they can offer daytime slots in April and May. A tutor who can only manage 8pm is the wrong match for the weeks that matter most.

faqs.question: He is awake until 2am and still behind. What is actually going wrong?
faqs.answer: Long hours with little output almost always mean the work has no sequence, not that there is too much of it. A Grade 12 student juggling applications, coursework and revision will default to whatever is most urgent that evening, which means the hardest subject gets pushed night after night. The fix is unglamorous: list everything outstanding with its real deadline, decide what gets dropped, and give the week a shape somebody else checks. A tutor can hold that structure, but a parent or the school counsellor can too, and it should happen before you add more tutoring hours.

faqs.question: Should we tutor two subjects or go deep on one in the final year?
faqs.answer: Go deep on one unless the offer names two. In a final year, two tutors mean two sets of homework, two schedules and a student attending more and finishing less. Pick the subject where a grade is most likely to move per hour of work, which is usually the one where the student knows the material but writes the wrong kind of answer. If a second subject genuinely cannot be ignored, a short fortnightly online session for question practice costs less time than a full second engagement and keeps the week survivable.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a short Grade 12 engagement?
faqs.answer: Short final-year engagements are often priced differently from year-long ones, and we will not quote figures that would be wrong across areas. What drives the rate is the level and scarcity of the subject, since Higher Level specialists who have taken students to final examinations are in demand precisely in this window; the travel involved, which is why a tutor crossing the creek or Ghodbunder Road charges for the commute; session length and frequency; and whether the arrangement is at home, online or hybrid. Ask two or three shortlisted tutors directly and compare what each session includes.

faqs.question: Our son is in Thane off Ghodbunder Road and his evening slot keeps collapsing in traffic. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than the tutor, if the tutor is good. Ghodbunder Road between Majiwada and Kasarvadavali defeats even careful planning in the evening peak, and the sessions that survive in Thane are weekend mornings and post-dinner ones after the worst of it clears. The other option is a hybrid week: one home session on Saturday morning and one online midweek, which removes the commute from the fragile slot entirely. If the tutor cannot do either, we can match you with someone already based on your side of Thane.

faqs.question: What if the tutor cannot continue right through to the examinations?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book, because a handover in the final month is genuinely damaging. We check availability through to study leave as part of matching, and we ask tutors to flag travel or other commitments in April and May. If a change becomes unavoidable, we move quickly and pass on the tutor's notes, the diagnostic from the first session and the work completed, so the replacement is not starting from a blank page. Even so, continuity in the last stretch is worth protecting, which is why the availability question belongs in your first conversation.

faqs.question: The school says predicted grades go out next month. What can we usefully do before then?
faqs.answer: Focus entirely on work the teacher will see, because that is what the prediction rests on. Find out from each subject teacher what is still to be submitted or assessed before the prediction is made, and put the student's effort there rather than into general revision. One well-finished piece of assessed work in the right subject is worth more at this moment than a fortnight of past papers. Ask the DP coordinator how the school forms predictions, and keep the request factual rather than adversarial. Schools respond to evidence, not to pressure.

sections.heading: Shortlisting a grade 5 IB PYP tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Grade 5 parents arrive with a different complaint from Grade 1 parents, and it is almost always about organisation rather than ability. The marks are acceptable. The teacher is not worried. But your son cannot start a task until someone breaks it into steps for him, he reads quickly and cannot tell you what the page said, and his folder is a landslide. That is the brief we match against, and it needs a tutor who is comfortable withdrawing help rather than one who is good at giving it. Most families here start by looking for an IB private tutor Mumbai agencies would call a general primary tutor, and then discover that senior primary home tuition is a different job with a different skill set.

The sequence is short. 1. You send the grade, the school and the one thing that is actually going wrong, in your own words. 2. We shortlist two or three PYP tutors who have taught the top of the primary school and who already work your corridor on the evenings you have free. 3. You call each of them for ten minutes and ask how they would handle your specific problem, not what their method is. 4. One paid diagnostic session runs at your flat. 5. You tell us yes, no, or try the other one, and we act on it the same week.

The ten-minute call matters more at this age than people expect, because the wrong tutor for a Grade 5 student is usually the one who is too helpful. A tutor who answers your question with a plan for making your son produce the plan himself is the one to take. A tutor who offers to go through his homework with him every evening is offering to extend the dependence you called about. A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai parents run at ten at night returns a list ordered by advertising, not by anyone who has made that distinction.

We also check availability honestly before the match rather than after it. A Grade 5 slot usually sits between seven and eight-thirty in the evening, which is a real advantage over the younger years and widens the field considerably. What kills these arrangements is not distance but the tutor who has taken on a Diploma Programme student at the same hour and begins treating your ten-year-old as the session that can be moved. Ask what else is in that slot. A good tutor will tell you.

sections.heading: Grade 5, the last year of the PYP, and what comes next
paragraphs: In most IB schools in Mumbai, Grade 5 is the final year of the Primary Years Programme, and what sits on the far side of the summer is the Middle Years Programme (MYP). The change is structural rather than cosmetic. Your child moves from a class teacher who knows everything about her to a timetable of subject specialists who each know one part. Assessment moves from continuous teacher judgement to published criteria with strands and command terms. The work starts arriving with instructions that assume she can read instructions.

That is the real content of a Grade 5 year, and it is why this year is worth taking seriously even when nothing looks wrong. The programme keeps its transdisciplinary shape, with units of inquiry pulling several subjects into one question, and it keeps the learner profile as the language teachers use about behaviour. What changes inside the year is the expected degree of independence: the same unit structure, with far more of the planning handed to the child. What you are hiring is a PYP transdisciplinary learning IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor Mumbai schools will recognise as working inside their own framework rather than against it.

Schools in this city differ on where the programme boundary falls and how the culminating exhibition project is scheduled, so your school's own calendar and your PYP coordinator are the authority on what your child faces and when. The exhibition has its own page on this site and its own specialists, and a Grade 5 tutor should be aware of it without letting it swallow the year. Anyone who tells you with certainty how many weeks it runs or how it is assessed, without checking your school's current documentation, is guessing on your behalf.

There are still no external examinations. Nothing a Grade 5 child does this year appears on a transcript. The thing worth protecting is therefore not a mark but a set of working habits, because those are what the MYP will immediately start charging for. IB home tuition in Mumbai at this level is best understood as buying one year of supervised practice at working alone, which sounds like a contradiction and is exactly the point.

sections.heading: What changes in Grade 5: from being taught to being asked
paragraphs: Four capabilities separate a Grade 5 student who will cope next year from one who will struggle, and none of them is content knowledge. Turning a long text into notes in her own words. Choosing between sources and saying why one was better. Running a multi-step problem without being told which step comes next. And breaking a two-week task into pieces with dates attached. Teachers describe these as study skills, which undersells them. They are the actual curriculum of the final primary year.

A worked example from a unit most Mumbai PYP classes run in some form. The inquiry is on how people move and settle, and the task is to find out why a family might leave one place for another and present what you found. A Grade 5 child reads three articles, understands all three, and produces a presentation that is a reordered copy of the longest one. She has not plagiarised deliberately; she has never been taught the difference between copying a sentence and making a point from it. That gap is invisible in Grade 4 and expensive in MYP Year 1, where sources must be acknowledged and the marking criteria notice.

Mathematics has its own Grade 5 pattern. Fractions, decimals and percentages stop being three topics and become one idea viewed three ways, and the child who never achieved real fluency with times tables now hides it successfully, because the problems have become wordy enough that the arithmetic is the small part. The tutor's job is diagnostic before it is remedial: find out whether the error is in reading the problem, choosing the operation, or executing it, because those are three different lessons and most Grade 5 maths tuition teaches only the third.

Language work shifts from writing more to writing with structure. A paragraph should have a point and evidence for it, a piece should have a beginning that is not a restatement of the title, and a child should be able to say what the reader is supposed to think at the end. A PYP transdisciplinary learning tutor in Mumbai working with this age should be asking your child what she is trying to say before correcting how she said it. The learner profile attributes that matter most now are thinker and principled, which look like checking an answer unprompted and naming the source you used. A home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning Mumbai parents engage in the final primary year should be working on all four of these capabilities at once, because the school will assume next year that somebody already did.
bullets: Notes in her own words, not highlighted lines from the text
Choosing between sources and saying which was better and why

sections.heading: Grade 5 home tuition across Mumbai, and why the radius widens
paragraphs: A ten-year-old can take a half past seven slot, and that single fact changes coverage completely compared with the younger primary years. The tutor is travelling after the worst of the evening peak rather than through it, so a grade 5 IB PYP tutor in Mumbai can reasonably be matched one suburb further away. It also means the scarce tutor, the one who genuinely understands the handover into the Middle Years Programme, is reachable for families who would never get them at five o'clock.

In South Mumbai we match around Worli, Breach Candy, Babulnath and Fort, and the Coastal Road plus Metro Line 3 have made the north-south runs on the island far less punishing than they were. The Bandra Worli Sea Link brings a Bandra West tutor to Worli for an eight o'clock start without drama, which is a genuinely new option for senior primary families. The Western Line and the Western Express Highway then carry the Western Suburbs, where Andheri West, Malad, Kandivali East and Dahisar East are well supplied and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have cut the Dahisar to Andheri journey to something a tutor will accept twice a week.

The Central and Eastern Suburbs are where the later slot helps most. Kanjurmarg, Bhandup West and Powai sit off JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway with no useful station for Powai itself, so these matches are made by road and the difference between a six o'clock and a half past seven departure is twenty minutes of tutor time. Govandi and Mulund East are served by the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Chembur or Wadala tutor reachable from the island city in a way the map hides. Metro Line 1 and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road fill in the east-west gaps that the suburban railway never covered.

Across the creek, Navi Mumbai is matched node to node: Belapur, Seawoods and Panvel each have their own supply, connected by Palm Beach Road and the Harbour Line, and the Atal Setu has shortened the island city link without making a weekday evening crossing sensible as a weekly commitment. In Thane, the Ghodbunder Road corridor out past Hiranandani Estate is the deciding factor, so Thane West families are matched to Thane tutors with Mulund as the occasional exception. PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes Mumbai families book hold for a full year when the tutor's own commute is boring, and break when it is heroic.

sections.heading: The Mumbai calendar in a Grade 5 year, month by month
paragraphs: The shape of the year in most Mumbai IB schools is two long terms either side of a Diwali break, opening soon after the monsoon sets in and closing for a long gap before the next academic year. Check your own school's calendar, since senior primary dates shift with conference and project scheduling and no two schools here agree. What is predictable is the rhythm of pressure, and in Grade 5 the pressure is clustered rather than spread.

The opening weeks are deceptively calm, which is when the handover work should actually start. By the middle of the first term the longer tasks begin, and this is when a child who cannot plan first becomes visible: the work is handed in complete and was finished the night before. The stretch after the Diwali break is the heaviest, with the culminating project work and the subject-style demands of the final primary term arriving together. The closing weeks turn towards transition, with information sessions about next year and, in many schools, conversations about subject and language choices for the Middle Years Programme.

The summer gap deserves its own sentence, because for Grade 5 it is not a risk but an opportunity. Between the last day of primary school and the first day of the MYP sits a long break in which nothing is assessed. It is the only time your child will ever have to practise note-taking and self-managed work with nothing at stake. Two short sessions a week through that gap do more for next year than a term of panic in October.

Families here come into Grade 5 from very different houses. A student at Oberoi International School in Goregaon East or Podar International School has been inside an IB primary school throughout. A student at NES International School in Mulund West or Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo may be in a school running several pathways, where the primary years and the later board route interact in ways that affect subject choices. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, we cannot speak for their placement decisions, and we do not guarantee grades or outcomes of any kind.

sections.heading: Can a ten-year-old actually learn online, or is home tuition still better?
paragraphs: A ten-year-old genuinely can work online, which is not true of a six-year-old, so this is a real choice rather than a formality. Home tutoring remains the lead recommendation for Grade 5 because the skills this year is about, planning, note-taking and folder discipline, live in physical objects a tutor needs to see and handle. Online works well as the second session of the week and becomes the better option outright in two specific situations described below. For most families in this city the sensible default is still weekly home tuition with online used around it.

The argument for in-person at this age is concrete. A tutor sitting beside your child can pick up the actual folder, find the three loose sheets in the wrong section, and make her file them. She can watch the order in which your daughter approaches a word problem, which is the diagnostic information that matters and is almost invisible on a screen. And a grade 5 IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai can see the desk your child really works at, with its school bag on the chair and its phone face up, and change it. None of that happens over a video call.

Online earns the slot when the skill being taught is verbal and quick, and when distance would otherwise rule out the right person. A twenty-minute midweek review of notes your child made herself works perfectly on a screen with a shared document. A scarce tutor who understands the MYP handover and lives in Thane can take a Panvel family online and never could in person. An IB online tutor in Mumbai also saves the session on the evening Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway stops moving, which over a year is several sessions rather than one.

Hybrid is the arrangement most senior primary families end up with, and the sensible split is one in-person session carrying the teaching and one online session carrying accountability. The honest warning about online at ten is that the second screen is always available: a child who is working in a browser is a click away from something else, and a parent who is not in the room will not know. Keep the online session short, keep it focused on work she has already produced, and sit within earshot for the first month.

sections.heading: What should I check myself before a tutor starts?
paragraphs: We verify identity documents, see qualifications rather than accept a list, and confirm the stated teaching history with a reference who actually supervised the person. For Grade 5 we look hardest for experience at the top of a primary school and, ideally, some exposure to what the Middle Years Programme expects, because a tutor who has only taught lower primary will teach your ten-year-old beautifully and prepare her for the wrong thing. Every grade 5 IB PYP tutor in Mumbai we put forward has cleared that check before you see the name.

What we cannot do is worth stating in plain words. We cannot run a state criminal records check, we are not present in your flat, and we have no way to confirm a result claimed at another family's house. We do not guarantee grades, placements or MYP subject outcomes, and there is nothing in the PYP to grade anyway. Parents often open the conversation by asking for the best IB tutor in Mumbai, and the useful reframing is to ask instead who has already walked a Grade 5 student into the Middle Years Programme and knows what broke. Be wary of any tutor who offers a guaranteed improvement by a date, because the honest answer at this age is that habits take a term to shift and cannot be promised on a calendar.

Your own checks are different at ten than at six, and they are about autonomy. In the first two sessions, listen for who is doing the thinking. If the tutor says what the next step is every time, the session is comfortable and useless. If she asks your daughter what she thinks the next step is and waits through the silence, that is the right person, even though the room sounds less productive. Also look at the end: does your child put her own things away and know what she is doing before the next session, or does the tutor hand you a list?

On access and logistics, settle the practical points in week one. Ask your society office to register the tutor as a recurring visitor for a named weekly slot rather than processing a gate pass every week. Decide where sessions happen and keep it consistent, because Grade 5 work needs space for a folder, a notebook and a laptop at the same time. And agree what happens to a missed session before one is missed, since the first cancellation in a Mumbai monsoon will happen in July.

sections.heading: What does a Grade 5 PYP home tuition session look like in Mumbai?
paragraphs: A Grade 5 session runs around an hour and is built back to front: it starts with what your child did alone since last week and ends with what she will do alone before next week. A workable shape is ten minutes reviewing her own notes and the task she set herself, fifteen minutes of teaching on whichever skill the last piece of work exposed, twenty minutes of her working while the tutor watches and says very little, ten minutes where she explains what she did and what she would change, and five minutes planning the week with dates written by her hand rather than the tutor's.

The twenty minutes of near-silence is the part that distinguishes senior primary tutoring from everything below it, and the part parents sometimes query because it looks like the tutor is being paid to sit. It is the only block in which anyone finds out what your child can do without a prompt. A tutor who fills that silence is destroying the information she came for. A grade 5 IB PYP home tuition session in Mumbai that never contains it will produce a child who performs well with an adult beside her and stalls in MYP Year 1 when no adult is.

One year either side the session is a different thing entirely. In Grade 4 the tutor still owns the structure: she decides the order, breaks every task into steps, and checks each one before the next, and that is correct for a nine-year-old. In MYP Year 1 the frame has moved again, to subject-specific work against published criteria, where a tutor is unpicking what a command term asks for and what evidence a strand wants, and self-management is assumed rather than taught. Grade 5 is the handover between those two, and the whole skill of teaching it is deciding each week what to stop doing.

Things a Grade 5 tutor should push back on. Finishing the project, in any form, including the version where the tutor types while the child dictates, because the culminating project exists to be the child's own and schools can tell. Teaching MYP content a year early, which substitutes vocabulary for capability. Running the session as homework supervision, which is the most commonly requested and least useful arrangement at this age. And filling the folder on the child's behalf, which fixes the symptom you can see and none of the habit you are paying for.
bullets: Around an hour, built backwards from what she did alone last week
Twenty minutes of her working while the tutor watches and stays quiet
She writes the week's plan, with dates, in her own hand

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one year: what should have changed
paragraphs: At four weeks the only honest measures are procedural, and they are easy to see if you know to look. Is the folder in order without you asking? Does she start a piece of work by writing down what it is asking for, rather than by writing the title in bubble letters? Does she come to the session with a question of her own? None of that will show up in marks yet, and the marks were probably acceptable when you called us, which is why marks are the wrong instrument this year.

At one term the output should move in three places. Notes should be in her own words and shorter than the source. A long task should be broken up on a calendar before it is started. And in maths she should be able to tell you which step of a multi-step problem she is unsure about, instead of saying she does not get it. Teacher comments usually shift from how she is settling to what she is producing and how she approaches it. If none of that has happened in a full term, change something, and say so rather than renewing because the tutor is pleasant.

At one year the test sits on the other side of the summer. The question is not what her final primary report said but whether she survives the first six weeks of the Middle Years Programme without a crisis: homework from five subject teachers arriving in the same week, criteria she has to read herself, and a long task with no checkpoints. Parents who get this year right usually report the same thing, which is that September was dull. Dull is the goal.

The limits are real and worth naming. A tutor cannot change a child who is not sleeping, and ten is the age at which devices start eating the evening. A tutor cannot substitute for an assessment: if your child reads fluently but cannot summarise anything, or if attention collapses on written work specifically, ask your school counsellor or a paediatrician about an evaluation rather than buying a third session. We do not guarantee grades or MYP placement, and no honest tutor will tell you otherwise in a city where every parent has heard someone promise it.
bullets: Four weeks: folder order, reading the question, bringing her own question
One term: shorter notes in her own words and a planned long task

sections.heading: Booking Grade 5 home classes in Mumbai
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first session and it will be diagnostic rather than introductory. The last report and any conference notes, so the tutor reads the school's words. One piece of recent work your child did badly, which is far more informative than her best piece. The folder, exactly as it is, unsorted. And one sentence from you about what actually happens at the desk, whether that is forty minutes of nothing, or constant questions, or work finished suspiciously fast.

Settle the timetable before the teaching starts. One longer weekday session plus one short online review is the pattern that suits this year group, and a half past seven start is usually easier to protect than a six o'clock one. Decide where the work will happen and clear it: Grade 5 needs a folder, a notebook and often a laptop open at the same time, so a dining table beats a cramped desk. Agree now what happens when a session is missed, because in a Mumbai monsoon one will be.

The first session should end with your child telling you what she is doing before the next one. If the tutor tells you instead, say something in week two rather than month three. The single best indicator in the first month is not progress on content, it is whether the amount of help in the room is going down. In a well-run Grade 5 year the tutor talks less in February than in July.

After that the arrangement should be quiet and legible. A short note after each session covering what was covered, what she did alone, and what to leave her to struggle with at home, which is the instruction parents find hardest and which matters most now. IB tuition fees in Mumbai vary with all the usual factors, and senior primary home tuition is no exception, so ask what the rate includes in terms of preparation and updates before you compare two tutors on price alone.
bullets: Bring the last report, a weak piece of work and the unsorted folder
One longer weekday session plus a short online review each week
A later start suits Grade 5 and is easier to protect than an early one
Judge the first month by how much help is being withdrawn

faqs.question: My son is in Grade 5, his marks are fine, but he cannot work without me sitting there. Is that a tuition problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most worthwhile Grade 5 brief there is. Dependence is invisible in a primary report because an attentive parent and a patient class teacher cover for it completely. It becomes visible in the first weeks of the Middle Years Programme, when five subject teachers set work in the same week and nobody breaks it into steps. A tutor working on this will deliberately make your son uncomfortable for a few weeks by refusing to name the next step. Expect sessions to look less productive and the work at home to improve.

faqs.question: Should we wait and get a tutor when the Middle Years Programme actually starts?
faqs.answer: Waiting is the common choice and usually the expensive one. Starting in MYP Year 1 means teaching self-management, note-taking and source use while the child is simultaneously being assessed against criteria for the first time, with real marks attached. Starting in Grade 5 means teaching the same things in a year where nothing is on a transcript and mistakes are free. The same work costs less and lands better twelve months earlier. If budget forces a choice, two short sessions a week in Grade 5 beat four a week in panic next October.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel out along Ghodbunder Road for an evening slot in Thane?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is based in Thane rather than crossing in from Mulund or the Western Suburbs. The Ghodbunder Road stretch past Hiranandani Estate towards Kasarvadavali behaves very differently at half past seven than at six, which is one advantage a Grade 5 slot has over a primary one. We still match within Thane wherever possible, because a tutor whose own travel is unremarkable keeps the slot for a full year and a tutor making an epic commute starts rescheduling by the second term.

faqs.question: Does a parent have to be at home, and should I sit in on Grade 5 sessions?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, but you should stop sitting in after the first two sessions, and that is a change from the younger years. A ten-year-old performs differently when a parent is listening, usually by asking the tutor fewer questions and you more. Stay within earshot for online sessions in the first month. Otherwise set them up at a cleared table, leave, and get your information from the session note rather than from overhearing. Your presence is the thing the year is trying to make unnecessary.

faqs.question: Our building wants a new gate entry for every visitor. Will that disrupt a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: It will cost you minutes off the start of every session unless you fix it in week one. Ask the society office to register the tutor as a recurring visitor against a named day and time, which most Mumbai complexes will do on a written request from a resident. Where a building insists on a fresh entry each visit, tell the tutor the realistic queue at the gate and the lift situation at that hour so the slot is planned around it. Five minutes lost weekly is close to a whole session over a term.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for Grade 5?
faqs.answer: Level, scarcity, travel, duration and mode, in roughly that order. Senior primary sits below Diploma Programme rates, but a tutor who genuinely understands the handover into the MYP is scarcer than a general primary tutor and priced accordingly. Travel distance and the hour of the slot matter because an evening crossing of the city costs the tutor more than the session length suggests. Session length, frequency and whether you choose in person, online or hybrid complete the picture. Ask what preparation and parent updates are included before comparing two rates.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the final primary exhibition project?
faqs.answer: Only at the edges, and you should be cautious of anyone who offers more. The culminating project is meant to be the child's own inquiry, schools supervise it closely, and work that arrives polished in an adult register is noticed. A tutor can legitimately teach the skills it draws on: turning a broad interest into an answerable question, keeping a research log, acknowledging sources, rehearsing a presentation out loud. The project itself has its own page and its own specialists on this site. For a general Grade 5 tutor it should be a small part of the year, not its centre.

faqs.question: She reads constantly and still cannot summarise a chapter. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Reading fluently and reading for meaning are different skills, and Grade 5 is where the gap between them shows. A child can decode every word at speed and still hold nothing, because nobody has taught her to stop at the end of a section and say what it was about. The fix is mechanical and boring: read a section, close the book, say it in one sentence, write that sentence. If that produces nothing after a few weeks of consistent practice, raise it with the school and ask whether a comprehension or attention evaluation is worth doing.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Grade 5 student need?
faqs.answer: Two is the normal answer and one can be enough. The useful pattern is one in-person session of about an hour and one short online review, because this year is about work the child does between sessions rather than work she does in them. More than two sessions a week usually means the tutor has become the structure, which is the opposite of the goal. If you are considering a third session, ask what she is doing alone instead. That question has saved several families a lot of money.

faqs.question: We are in Powai and the tutor commutes from Ghatkopar. Is that going to last a year?
faqs.answer: It usually does for a Grade 5 slot and often does not for a younger one. Powai has no station of its own, so everything arrives by road off JVLR, and a Ghatkopar tutor taking a half past seven start is travelling after the worst of it. The same tutor at five o'clock is a different proposition. Ask the tutor directly how long the journey takes at your slot time and what their fallback is when it goes wrong, then hold the online option in reserve for those evenings rather than cancelling.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my daughter has not warmed to her?
faqs.answer: Tell us, because at ten this matters more than it does at six. A Grade 5 student who does not want to look foolish in front of a particular adult will simply stop attempting anything difficult, which makes the whole arrangement pointless while looking perfectly calm from outside. Give it three or four sessions, since some of the discomfort is the handover itself and is meant to be there. If she is still going quiet rather than wrong, we shortlist someone else without you starting again.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring through the summer break before MYP?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value window of the whole year. Nothing is assessed, no homework is competing for the evening, and the skills that MYP Year 1 immediately demands can be practised with zero consequences for failing at them. Two short sessions a week through the break, built around note-taking from real texts and planning a self-chosen project with dates, buy more than a term of catching up in October. It is also the one time a tutor can let your child fail at something properly, which is how self-management is actually learned.

sections.heading: How do you find a grade 6 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai who understands Year 1?
paragraphs: You describe the first term, not the subject. A grade 6 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai is matched on one question: is this child struggling with the material, or with the way Middle Years Programme tasks are written? Those two problems look identical on a report card and need opposite tutors. The first needs a subject teacher. The second needs someone who can sit with a task sheet and translate it.

The reason this distinction matters so much in Grade 6 is that Year 1 of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is the year the assessment language changes. A child who spent primary school being marked on whether the answer was right now gets marked against criteria A to D, where the same correct answer can score high on one strand and low on another. Parents describe the symptom as careless work. It is almost never carelessness. It is a student who answered the question they thought was being asked.

So the intake conversation goes through artefacts rather than adjectives. We ask for two or three marked tasks, the current timetable, and the name of the school, because an Ecole Mondiale World School Year 1 task sheet and a Podar International School one are structured differently even when the subject group is the same. From those, the match is narrowed to tutors who have taught that entry year and who live close enough to hold a standing weekly slot through a Mumbai monsoon.

What you get back is a shortlist, not a single name. Each tutor on it has taught MYP Year 1 within the last few years, has been identity-checked, and can reach your address at the time you asked for without a ninety-minute commute in each direction. You choose. If the first one does not fit your child, you say so and the next one comes from the same shortlist rather than from a fresh search.

sections.heading: Where Grade 6 sits in the IB Middle Years Programme across Mumbai
paragraphs: In most Mumbai schools Grade 6 is MYP Year 1, the first year of the Middle Years Programme and the first year after the Primary Years Programme (PYP). That single fact explains most of what a parent notices in the first term. The child moves from one or two class teachers to a separate specialist for every subject group, each with their own task sheets, their own deadlines and their own idea of what a good answer looks like.

Some Mumbai schools do not run MYP Year 1 at all and begin the programme in Grade 7 or Grade 8, with a school-designed middle school before it. Others run a full continuum and your child has been in the IB system since kindergarten. A MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai parents book for Grade 6 therefore has to establish one thing first: which year of the programme the school actually calls this, because a child in a school-designed Grade 6 is not being marked on MYP criteria yet and tutoring them as if they are wastes the term.

Establish which course your child is entered for before anything else. Ask the Middle Years Programme coordinator, in writing, which MYP year group Grade 6 corresponds to at your school, which subject groups are assessed against published criteria this year, and whether reports carry criterion levels or percentages. Schools answer this in a sentence. Two of our commonest first-session corrections come from parents who assumed one and got the other.

Nothing in Grade 6 locks a pathway. No tier is entered, no option block closes, and the Diploma Programme (DP) is five years away. What Year 1 decides is narrower and more important than that: whether your child can read a command term and a criterion strand without help. Every tier decision, every option choice and every internal assessment in the years above rests on that skill, and this is the only year where it is the explicit job.

sections.heading: The MYP subject groups a Grade 6 student meets in the first term
paragraphs: Year 1 introduces the subject groups all at once: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each is assessed against criteria labelled A to D, and the strands behind those letters are written differently in every subject group. Check the current MYP subject guide for your child's subjects rather than assuming the criteria carry the same meaning across them, because the IB revises these guides on its own cycle.

The two groups that surprise Grade 6 parents most are Design and Language Acquisition. Design is assessed as a process, so a beautiful final product with no documented investigation or evaluation scores badly, and a modest product with a well-evidenced process scores well. Many Mumbai parents see their first low mark here and read it as a mark for craft. It is a mark for the research and evaluation stages the student skipped. A MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai working with Year 1 spends more time on the design folder than on the artefact.

Language Acquisition is the other one. New Grade 6 entrants are placed in a language phase, and the phase is a judgement about where the student currently is, not a grade. A child placed in an early phase for French or Spanish is not behind. A child placed too high because of a confident interview will drift for two terms before anyone notices. Ask which phase your child sits in, and what evidence placed them there, in the first month.

Individuals and Societies and Sciences both ask Year 1 students to do something primary school rarely did: cite where a claim came from and say how reliable it is. This is the single most common gap we see in Grade 6 home classes. The student knows the content, writes a confident paragraph, and loses the strand that asked for evidence. A tutor fixes this with the student's own marked work rather than with worksheets, which is why those marked tasks matter at intake.

sections.heading: Grade 6 IB MYP home classes in Mumbai zone by zone
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six tutoring markets that happen to share a municipal boundary, and for a Grade 6 student the practical consequence is bedtime. A Year 1 child cannot absorb a 9pm session, so the match has to be close enough that the tutor arrives at six or half past six. In South Mumbai that means matching within the island. A tutor coming down to Colaba or Cuffe Parade from the suburbs is crossing Peddar Road in the evening peak, and the Coastal Road helps the Worli stretch far more than it helps the last two kilometres.

In the Western Suburbs the rule is to match along the Western Line rather than across it. A tutor in Khar West reaches Juhu or Santacruz West quickly on Link Road, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made Malad to Kandivali East viable on a weekday. Pulling the same tutor east across the Western Express Highway at 6pm is where standing slots break down by the third week. The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so Powai tutors are reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Wadala up through Vikhroli to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway makes the island city far closer from Chembur than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node across Vashi, Nerul and Belapur on Palm Beach Road, and the Atal Setu has changed what is possible from the island without making a weekday Grade 6 slot across the creek sensible. In Thane, Ghodbunder Road sets the schedule: Pokhran Road and Majiwada are twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour at seven in the evening.

Those are the reasons grade 6 IB MYP home classes in Mumbai are matched by corridor and not by postcode. A home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai families keep for a full year is almost always one who travels fifteen or twenty minutes, not one who was the strongest name on a list. Parents searching IB tutors near me Mumbai are, correctly, searching for durability rather than distance.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school calendar does to a Year 1 student
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB school year opens in June, and for a Grade 6 student the first pressure point arrives earlier than parents expect. Schools front-load Year 1 with introductory units that end in the first assessed criterion tasks around August, which means the first evidence that something is wrong lands before the monsoon break rather than after it. Families who wait for the first formal report in late autumn have already lost a term in which the problem was cheap to fix.

Families across the city deal with slightly different versions of this. Children at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu come up through a full PYP continuum, so the criterion language is less of a shock and the Year 1 jump is mostly about having eight teachers. Students entering Oberoi International School at Goregaon East off JVLR or Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo from a national-curriculum primary school meet both changes at once. At Podar International School in Santacruz and Powai, and at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Grade 6 cohorts routinely mix both kinds of student in one classroom, which is why a Year 1 teacher cannot pitch the first unit at everyone.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. We name these schools because their calendars set the assessment pressure points our tutors schedule around, and because a tutor who has worked with students from a particular school knows how its task sheets are written. Nothing more is implied by the mention.

The practical calendar advice for Grade 6 is to use the quiet months. June and July are the only window in Year 1 where a tutor can work on reading task sheets without a deadline in the room. By the time the second term opens in January the student is carrying real coursework, and remediation competes with it. IB home tuition in Mumbai booked in the first half of the year is doing different work from the same tutor booked in February, even with the same child.

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better for a Grade 6 MYP student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For Grade 6, home tuition is the default and the reason is attention span rather than technology. A ten or eleven year old in Year 1 needs someone physically beside them to stop the drift, to turn the task sheet over, and to notice that the child has written three sentences in twenty minutes. A grade 6 IB MYP home tutor in Mumbai also sees the things a camera does not: the unopened planner, the folder with loose sheets, the tablet open on another tab. That is most of the diagnosis in Year 1.

Online works at this age in two specific situations. The first is scarcity: if your child needs a tutor for a less common Language Acquisition phase or a specific Arts strand, an IB online tutor in Mumbai or elsewhere in India may be the only person who has actually taught it. The second is the monsoon. Keeping a session online through a week of heavy rain on the Western Express Highway is far better than cancelling it, and a student who has already built a relationship in person transfers to a screen easily.

Hybrid is what most Grade 6 families settle into by the second term without planning it. One in-person session a week carries the diagnostic work and the folder discipline, and a shorter online check-in mid-week carries the follow-up on whatever was set. This also protects the booking against the two things that break standing slots in Mumbai: evening traffic and school events that move without notice.

The honest trade-off is that online at this age depends entirely on the adult at home for the first month. A Grade 6 student will not set up the camera at the right angle, will not have the marked task on the desk, and will not say that they did not understand. Nobody should promise that an online arrangement with an unsupervised ten year old will work as well as someone sitting next to them, because it generally does not.

sections.heading: How Grade 6 tutors are checked before they ring your doorbell
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform is identity-verified from government photo identification, has their degree and teaching qualifications checked against the issuing institution where that is possible, and gives a teaching history we contact rather than read. For a Grade 6 match we add one filter: the tutor has to have taught the entry year of the Middle Years Programme, not just the programme. A tutor who has taught MYP Year 5 brilliantly may have no idea how to explain a criterion strand to a ten year old.

There are checks only you can do, and for a Year 1 student they matter more than anything on our side. Watch the first session if you can. A good grade 6 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai spends the first half of it reading your child's marked task with them and asking what they thought the question wanted. A weaker one opens a textbook at chapter one. Ask your child afterwards what they were asked to explain back, because a Year 1 student who was never asked to explain anything was being lectured.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, promises to finish the year's syllabus by December, or wants to do the Design folder with your child rather than beside them. At this age the academic honesty line is easy to cross by being helpful. The tutor's job is to make the student produce the work, and an adult who hands over wording is teaching the child that the work is not theirs.

On our side, nothing about verification is a promise about outcomes. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will either. What verification buys you is a stranger at your door whose identity and teaching record are known, which is the part a parent cannot check alone at six on a weekday evening.

sections.heading: Why does a Grade 6 child with good work get low criterion marks?
paragraphs: Because the task asked for something the work never attempted. This is the defining Grade 6 problem and it is worth being concrete. A Year 1 Individuals and Societies task asks the student to describe a change and to evaluate the sources used. The student writes two accurate, neatly organised pages describing the change, says nothing about where the information came from, and is marked strongly on one criterion and near the bottom of another. The parent sees a low overall mark on work that looks careful and concludes the teacher is harsh.

The fix is mechanical and it is the main thing a Year 1 tutor should be doing. Take the task sheet. Underline each command term: describe, outline, explain, evaluate. Next to each, write which criterion strand it belongs to. Then check the child's draft against that list and find the strand with no sentences pointing at it. A Grade 6 student can learn to do this in six or seven weeks, and once they can, the same child's marks move without any new subject content being taught.

The second pattern is the opposite. A student writes about everything, including strands the task never asked for, and runs out of time. In Design this shows up as a student who builds the product first and backfills an investigation that reads invented. In Language and Literature it shows up as plot summary where analysis was asked for. Both are reading failures rather than ability failures, which is why grade 6 IB MYP tuition in Mumbai aimed at this year group should be measured in task sheets decoded, not chapters covered.

What this means for fees is that the work is diagnostic rather than extensive. What IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is the subject's scarcity, the tutor's experience with this specific year group, how far they travel to you, the session length and whether the slot is peak evening or a weekend morning. A Year 1 engagement is often shorter than parents expect, because once the student reads tasks independently the reason for the booking has gone. We would rather say that than sell a year.

sections.heading: What progress looks like after a month of home tutoring in Year 1
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. You should be looking at whether your child can tell you what a task is asking for before they start it. That is the whole four-week test for Grade 6. If your child can hold up a task sheet and say that this part wants a description and this part wants an evaluation, the tutoring is working even if the next mark is identical to the last one. Criterion marks lag the skill by a reporting cycle.

At one term, expect two things. The work should arrive in the right shape for the task, and the folder should exist. Organisation is an outcome in Year 1, not an administrative detail, because a child who cannot find last week's feedback cannot act on it. If after a full term the drafts still miss whole strands, the problem is either the match or something outside the sessions, and that is a conversation to have rather than a reason to add a second subject.

At one full year, the honest measure is independence. A Grade 6 student who needed a tutor to decode every task in June should be decoding most of them alone by the following April, with the tutor moving to subject content or stepping back. Any arrangement that has the same child equally dependent twelve months later has failed at its actual job, whatever the marks say.

The limits are worth stating plainly. A tutor cannot make a ten year old care about a subject group they have decided they dislike, cannot replace sleep, and cannot compensate for a timetable with no free evenings. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and we do not publish success rates, because a figure like that would say nothing about your child. What we will do is tell you when we think a booking has stopped earning its place.

sections.heading: Starting Grade 6 MYP home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have three things ready and the first session is worth four. First, two or three marked Grade 6 tasks with the teacher's comments still on them, from different subject groups if you have them. Second, the current school timetable, so the tutor knows which days carry three assessed subjects. Third, the name of the school and the year group the school itself uses, because that settles whether your child is being marked on MYP criteria yet.

The first session with a Year 1 student follows a fixed shape. The tutor reads one marked task with your child and asks them to explain what they thought it wanted. They compare that against what the criteria actually asked for. They pick the single weakest strand and do one short piece of work on it, in the session, with the child writing. Nothing is sent home for the first week beyond one specific habit, usually a filing habit.

You then get a written note: which subject groups look secure, which criterion strands are weak, whether this is a content problem or a reading problem, and what the tutor proposes for the next three weeks. If that note does not match what you see at home, say so before session two. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents keep for a year is normally one who got corrected in the first fortnight and changed approach.

If the match is wrong, tell us in the first three weeks rather than at the end of term. We go back to the same shortlist, and the next tutor starts with the note from the first one, so your child does not repeat the diagnostic. Changing a tutor early costs a fortnight. Leaving a wrong match in place for a term costs a term.

faqs.question: My child was a strong student in Grade 5. Why have the marks dropped in Grade 6?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the marking changed, not the child. Grade 5 work was usually marked on whether the answer was correct. MYP Year 1 work is marked against criteria A to D, where a correct, well-written answer can still miss the strand that asked for evaluation or for evidence of sources. Your child is answering the question they think is being asked. Look at one marked task and find a criterion with nothing in the work pointing at it, and you will usually see the whole pattern in five minutes. This is a reading problem and it responds quickly to tutoring aimed at task decoding.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Grade 6 MYP student actually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the right starting point for a Year 1 student, and two is already a lot. At this age the limiting factor is attention and sleep rather than hours of instruction. A single well-run session that works on a real marked task, plus one small habit to practise, changes more than three sessions of general revision. Families who start with three sessions across three subject groups usually find by the second month that the same underlying skill was missing in all three. Start with one subject, fix the task-reading, then decide whether a second was ever needed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Powai for a 6pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and Powai is the clearest example of why matching happens by road rather than by rail. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar via JVLR, and a 6pm arrival is realistic for someone starting that journey within those areas. Pulling a tutor from the Western Suburbs across the Western Express Highway at that hour is not, which is why that match rarely survives a term. Give us your society name and the exact slot you want, and we shortlist tutors whose journey holds up in evening traffic.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home during a Grade 6 home tuition session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not in the room. Two reasons, both practical. A ten or eleven year old will not interrupt an adult to say they did not understand, so a parent passing through and asking what today's task was keeps the session honest. The second reason is simple safety: a tutor you have known for three weeks is still a stranger to your child. A grandparent or a regular member of household staff at home is enough. What does not work is an unsupervised Year 1 student with a tutor and a closed door.

faqs.question: What does a grade 6 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai charge, and what changes the rate?
faqs.answer: We do not publish a rate, because the honest answer is that it varies more than any single figure would suggest. The factors are consistent: how scarce the subject group is, how much experience the tutor has with this exact year group, how far they travel to reach you, how long the session runs, and whether you want a peak weekday evening or a weekend morning. A Year 1 booking is also often shorter than parents plan for, since the task-reading work has a natural end. Ask for the rate and the expected number of weeks together, then compare tutors on both.

faqs.question: My child has just moved from a CBSE school in Chembur into MYP Year 1. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with the two changes separately, because a transfer student meets both at once. The first is structural: a specialist teacher for every subject group instead of one class teacher, with deadlines arriving from several directions. The second is the criterion marking, which no national-curriculum primary school prepares a child for. Fix the organisational change first, in the first fortnight, with a folder and a single place where task sheets live. Then work on task decoding. Transfer students in Chembur and Wadala often also need Language Acquisition support, since continuum classmates may have had years of French or Spanish already.

faqs.question: Is it too early in Grade 6 to think about the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a set of choices, and no, as a set of habits. No Diploma Programme decision is made or constrained in Year 1, and a tutor who talks to a Grade 6 parent about Higher Level subjects is selling something. What does carry forward is the ability to read what an assessment task wants, cite where a claim came from, and keep work where it can be found. Those three habits are what a Diploma Programme student uses on an Internal Assessment five years later. Build them now because they are cheap to build at this age.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we go back to the same shortlist rather than starting a new search. There is no argument about it and no period of notice to serve. Three weeks is roughly the right moment to judge a Year 1 match, because by then you have seen whether the tutor opens your child's marked work or a textbook. The replacement starts with the written note from the first tutor, so the diagnostic is not repeated and your child is not asked the same questions again. Changing early costs a fortnight. Waiting until the term ends costs the term.

faqs.question: Does my Grade 6 child need a tutor for every MYP subject group?
faqs.answer: No, and booking by subject group is the commonest expensive mistake in Year 1. When a Grade 6 student is scoring low in Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Design at the same time, the shared cause is usually one skill rather than three content gaps: they are not reading what the criteria ask for. One tutor working on that in a single subject group tends to move the others, because the student starts applying the same habit everywhere. Book one subject, give it six weeks, and only add a second if the improvement genuinely does not transfer.

faqs.question: How does Language Acquisition phase placement work for a new Grade 6 student?
faqs.answer: The school places your child in a phase based on where their language currently is, and it is a starting point rather than a verdict. Confirm two things in the first month: which phase your child is in, and what evidence placed them there. A confident interview can place a student too high, after which they drift quietly for two terms. Being placed in an early phase is not a problem to fix with tutoring. Being placed above where the student actually is, is. Ask the coordinator directly, and check the current MYP guide for how phases work at your school.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and both parents work late. Can sessions run in the evening or at a weekend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Navi Mumbai the weekend option is often the better one. Kharghar tutors are matched from within the Navi Mumbai nodes, so a Vashi, Nerul or Belapur tutor reaches you along Palm Beach Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway without a creek crossing. A later weekday slot is possible, but a 9pm start with a Year 1 student rarely produces useful work whatever the tutor does. Most Kharghar families with two working parents settle on a weekend morning session plus a short mid-week online check, which keeps the pattern weekly without a late night.

faqs.question: Should a Grade 6 tutor be doing the work alongside my child, or watching them do it?
faqs.answer: Watching them do it, and this is the line to hold from Year 1 onwards. A helpful adult who suggests the wording, sketches the Design investigation or structures the paragraph has produced work that is not your child's, and in the Middle Years Programme that is an academic honesty issue as much as a learning one. The right pattern is the tutor asking what the criterion wants, the student writing a sentence, and the tutor saying whether it lands. It feels slower in session three. By session ten the student is doing it without being asked.

sections.heading: Matching a grade 7 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai to the right problem
paragraphs: The Year 2 request almost never arrives as a subject. It arrives as a sentence like: she understands it in class but the work goes in half-finished. So the first job of matching a grade 7 IB MYP tutor in Mumbai is to work out which of three different problems you have, because they need three different people. Problem one is a content gap in a specific subject group. Problem two is scheduling, where the student cannot run two long tasks at once. Problem three is quality control, where the work gets done but nobody checks it against the criteria before it goes in.

We separate them with the planner rather than the report card. Ask your child to open their planner or school portal and show you the next fortnight. If three assessed tasks sit in the same five days, you have a scheduling problem and a tutor who only teaches content will not touch it. If the tasks are spread and the marks are still low in one subject group, that is the content gap. If the work is finished early and still misses strands, it is quality control.

The shortlist is then built against that answer. A scheduling match means a tutor who runs the first twenty minutes of every session on the coming fortnight and will not open a textbook until that is done. A content match means subject depth in that group. A quality-control match means somebody who marks your child's draft against the published criteria in front of them, out loud, which is uncomfortable for a twelve year old and is the thing that works.

Everyone on the shortlist is identity-verified and has taught Middle Years Programme students in this middle band of the programme, which is a different skill from teaching Year 1 or Year 5. They also have to reach your address at the hour you asked for, repeatedly, through a Mumbai winter and a Mumbai monsoon. A tutor who is right on paper and arrives late every third week is not a match in Year 2, because the entire point of the booking is rhythm.

sections.heading: What MYP Year 2 asks of a Grade 7 student in Mumbai
paragraphs: Grade 7 is MYP Year 2 in most Mumbai IB schools, and it is the year the programme stops being new. The criteria are no longer unfamiliar, the specialist teachers are known, and the novelty excuse has expired. What replaces it is volume. Tasks in different subject groups now run for two or three weeks each and they are not coordinated with one another, so for the first time your child has to hold more than one piece of long work in their head at once.

Some Mumbai schools begin the Middle Years Programme at Grade 7 rather than Grade 6, which makes this a transfer year for part of the cohort and a second year for the rest. If your child is new to the programme this year, they are meeting criterion marking at the same time as the Year 2 workload, and that combination is harder than either alone. Establish which course your child is actually entered for by asking the coordinator which MYP year group Grade 7 maps to at your school, and whether your child is treated as a continuing or an entering student.

A MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai families book in Year 2 therefore starts with the school's own structure rather than with a generic middle school plan. Schools differ in how many subject groups they assess formally in this year, how they report, and when the interdisciplinary work happens. Check the current MYP guide and your school's assessment policy instead of relying on what an older sibling experienced two years ago.

Nothing is chosen in Year 2 and no tier is entered. What this year decides is whether the student can carry a load without an adult holding it for them. The students who struggle in MYP Year 4 are very often not the ones who were weak at content in Year 2. They are the ones whose parents were still managing their deadlines in Year 2 and stopped being able to by Year 4, when the work went beyond what a parent can usefully track.

sections.heading: Subject groups in Year 2: the interdisciplinary unit changes the week
paragraphs: The structural novelty of Year 2 for most Mumbai students is interdisciplinary work: a unit assessed across two subject groups at once, with its own criteria, run by two teachers who each see half of it. Students treat it as two separate assignments and lose the strands that ask them to connect the disciplines. Parents treat it as a project and underestimate it. Ask your school when the interdisciplinary unit falls and what it is assessed against, and check the current IB documentation for how your school structures it, because practice varies school to school.

The Approaches to Learning skills also become explicit in this year group. Schools report on categories including self-management, communication, research, thinking and social skills, and in Year 2 the self-management category is the one that predicts the next three years. A student who cannot break a three-week Sciences investigation into weekly pieces will produce it in the final two days, and the criteria that ask for a planned method will mark that honestly. This is the single most useful thing home tuition can work on at this age.

Language Acquisition in Year 2 brings phase movement into play. A student placed in an early phase on entry may be ready to move up, and a student placed optimistically in Year 1 is now visibly out of depth. Mumbai schools handle this differently and the decision usually sits with the department rather than the parent. What a tutor can do is produce evidence: a folder of the student's own work across a term that shows what they can actually do unaided in French, Spanish, Hindi or German.

Across Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies and the Arts, Year 2 raises the demand from describing to explaining. The command terms shift, and a student who scored well in Year 1 by writing clear, accurate description will suddenly plateau. Grade 7 home tuition that notices this shift early is worth more than extra content coverage, because the student needs a new sentence pattern rather than more facts. A MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai working at this level should be able to show you that pattern on your child's own paragraph.

In-person makes it easy to let the tutor carry the organisation rather than teaching the student to. Neither mode fixes that by itself. sections.heading: Why do Grade 7 marks move up and down in the same subject?
paragraphs: Because different tasks in the same subject group assess different criteria, and your child is strong on some strands and weak on others. This is the defining Year 2 pattern and it is entirely diagnosable. Take four marked Sciences tasks from one term. One was an investigation, one a written explanation, one a data analysis, one a reflection. The student scores well on two and badly on two, the term average lands in the middle, and the report says inconsistent. Nothing about the student is inconsistent. The tasks were testing different things.

Here is the worked version. A Grade 7 student in Chembur gets a strong mark on a Sciences task that asks her to explain a process, because explaining is what she does well. Three weeks later the task asks her to design a method and identify variables, and she loses most of that criterion because she has never been taught to lay out a method in the form the criteria expect. Both marks are in the same subject, in the same term, from the same teacher. The remedy is not more Sciences. It is twenty minutes on what a method section has to contain.

This is why a tutor who works from marks alone is useless in Year 2 and a tutor who works from the mark sheet breakdown is valuable. Ask the school for the criterion-level detail behind each task rather than the overall figure, then lay the tasks side by side. The pattern is usually obvious within four tasks, and it names the two strands worth working on for the rest of the year.

The second Year 2 pattern is the late submission that nobody logged. Work handed in two days late is marked, and the mark reflects a draft that was never checked. Parents see a subject-knowledge problem where there is a calendar problem. This is also where fees come in: what IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is the subject's scarcity, the tutor's experience with this year group, travel distance, session length and whether you want a peak evening slot. A Year 2 booking aimed at scheduling and strand coverage is usually a shorter engagement than one aimed at a content gap, and we will say which one we think you have.

sections.heading: How soon should a Year 2 student stop missing deadlines?
paragraphs: Inside three weeks, and that is the measure to hold us to. The first thing a Year 2 booking should change is not a mark. It is that every assessed task gets submitted on the day it was due, in a form the student had time to check. If that has not happened by the third session, the match or the routine is wrong, and adding a second subject will make it worse rather than better.

At one term the measure becomes strand coverage. Pull the criterion detail from the term's tasks and look for the two strands that were weak in week one. If those have moved and new weak strands have appeared elsewhere, that is normal progress and the work is continuing. If the same two strands are still weak after a term of weekly sessions, something is being worked around rather than fixed, and the right response is a conversation about the match.

At one exam cycle, the realistic outcome is a student who writes their own fortnight plan without being told, keeps a folder they can find things in, and reads a task sheet without an adult. Those are the three Year 2 outcomes, and they are what makes Year 4 survivable. Marks follow them, usually by one reporting cycle, and sometimes not in every subject group.

The limits matter here. A tutor cannot stop a twelve year old from leaving a task until the last evening if nothing at home changes at the same time, cannot compensate for a week with three performances and two tests, and cannot add hours to a Thursday. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rate, because any such figure would be about other people's children. What we will tell you is when a weekly slot has stopped doing useful work.

faqs.question: My Grade 7 child understands the work but keeps submitting it late. Is a tutor the right answer?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is matched to that problem rather than to the subject. faqs.question: What exactly is an interdisciplinary unit, and does my child need help with it?
faqs.answer: It is a unit assessed across two subject groups at once, with criteria that reward connecting the two disciplines rather than handling each separately. Most Grade 7 students lose marks on it by submitting what amounts to two unrelated assignments. Help is worth it only if the student does not understand that the connection itself is being assessed, which takes one session to establish. Ask your school when the unit falls, which subject groups are paired, and what it is assessed against, then check the current IB documentation rather than assuming it works the same way as last year's.

Sitting through the session changes your child's behaviour in it and gives the tutor an audience, which is not what you are paying for. If you want to watch a full session, watch the first one, then step back deliberately.

What is worth doing is keeping a quiet record across the year of which subject groups produce work your child does willingly and which produce work extracted under protest. That record is far more useful than a report average when option choices are discussed later, because by then the conversation moves fast and memory is unreliable.

First, criterion marking, where the correct answer does not automatically earn the mark if the strand asked for something else. Second, the Year 2 workload, with several long tasks running in parallel. Continuing students met the first in Grade 6 and only have the second to handle. Start with the criteria, using marked work rather than explanation, and get the folder and planner working in the first fortnight. faqs.question: What are Approaches to Learning skills and why does the school report on them?
faqs.answer: They are the transferable skills the Middle Years Programme teaches alongside subject content, grouped into categories that include self-management, communication, research, thinking and social skills. Schools report on them because they predict later performance better than Year 2 subject marks do. For a Grade 7 parent the one to watch is self-management. A student who cannot break a long task into weekly pieces will keep producing work written in the last two days, and the criteria that ask for a planned approach will mark that accurately for the next four years.

faqs.question: My child says the tutor just does the same thing the school does. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and it is a sign the match is wrong. A Year 2 tutor repeating the lesson adds a fourth hour of the same input, and a twelve year old will correctly describe that as pointless. The session should look different from school: the student's own marked work on the table, the criteria next to it, the student writing and the tutor questioning. If three sessions have gone by and your child cannot tell you what was different about them, raise it with us rather than waiting for the next report.

One tutor working across Individuals and Societies, Language and Literature and Sciences sees that pattern and fixes it once.
